claim: Adversarial audit verdict: in an S_4 tournament on 52 vertices no tight pair has J <= 5. Every audited step is justified: the identities (I1), sum e_y = 14 - J, the pair identity, the triple-excess formula, the Ex formula, sum_v s(u,v) = 2Ex(u); Lemma A at N = 52; c(u,v) >= 1; research/N52_TIGHT_J_GE_6.md sections 1 and 2; the J = 3, J = 4 analysis of R1-C (as corrected inside R1-C); the s <= 3, J = 5 analysis of R3-C; and the R4-C classification at J = 5, s = 4 on which section 1 depends. No step is false. Three presentational gaps are recorded and closed here: (G1) R1-C takes J <= 2 from Lemma J (one author, one checker); a direct N = 52 argument for J <= 2 is supplied, so the chain no longer needs Lemma J. (G2) Section 2 of the note concludes 'J = 5 is impossible' after treating only s = 5; that conclusion also needs s <= 3 (R3-C) and s = 4 (section 1 + R4-C), which are not cited there. (G3) In section 2 the sub-cases 5+4, 5+2+2, 4+4+1 fix the placement of the miss-sets using tau_u <= 5 without saying so. Every row of research/compute/n52_pairlevel.py is a valid consequence of S_4 at N = 52; no row is unjustified. A solver-free exhaustive enumeration (research/compute/r8a_vplus_enum.py) finds no survivor for J <= 5 with c >= 1. This is an order-52 tight-pair statement only; f(4) >= 53 is not proved and Erdos 902 is not solved.
definitions: T has S_4 on V, |V| = 52. P = {a, b}, a -> b, tight: R = D(P), |R| = 11. O = V \ (P u R), |O| = 39. For y in O: Q_y = R n N^-(y) (vertices of R beating y), q_y = |Q_y|, M_y = R \ Q_y (vertices of R beaten by y), e_y = q_y - 5. For r in R: d^-(r) = 25 + j_r, J = sum j_r, V_0 = {j = 0}, V_+ = R \ V_0, s = |V_+|. c(u,v) = #{w in R : w -> u, w -> v}. E_both(u,v) = sum_{y : u,v in M_y} e_y. tau_u = sum_{y : u in M_y} e_y. s(u,v) = sum_{w in R\{u,v}} (|D({u,v,w})| - 5). Ex(u) = sum over the 45 triples {u,v,w} in R of (|D| - 5). lambda(q) = 10 - C(10 - q, 2): lambda(5..10) = 0, 4, 7, 9, 10, 10. Inputs used without re-proof: (F1) every triple has >= 5 dominators (Lemma 1.2 of proof/ERDOS902_PROOF.md with n = 4). Everything else is re-derived below from (F1), S_4 on the single 4-set {a,b,u,v}, and tightness.
argument:
STEP 1. Re-derivation at N = 52.
(0) Basic structure. Every r in R beats a and b, so a, b are not in-neighbours of anything in R. For y in O, the dominators of {a,b,y} beat a and b, hence lie in D(P) = R, and beat y: D({a,b,y}) = Q_y, so q_y >= 5 by (F1), i.e. |M_y| = 6 - e_y <= 6. For r in R, D({a,b,r}) = R n N^-(r), so every in-degree of T[R] is >= 5; the in-degrees of T[R] sum to C(11,2) = 55 = 11*5, so T[R] is 5-regular. Justified.
(I1) d^-(r) = 5 (from R) + #{y in O : y -> r} (a, b do not beat r). So #{y : r in M_y} = d^-(r) - 5 = 20 + j_r. Justified.
(Sum e) sum_y |M_y| = sum_r (20 + j_r) = 220 + J; |M_y| = 6 - e_y, so 234 - sum e_y = 220 + J, sum e_y = 14 - J. Justified.
(Pair identity) A dominator of {u,v} (u,v in R) is not a or b; inside R it is a common in-neighbour (c of them); in O it is a y with u,v in M_y. |D(u,v)| = c + #{y : u,v in M_y}. Justified.
(c <= 4) If u -> v, every common in-neighbour lies in N^-(v) n R \ {u}, which has 4 elements. Justified.
(Triple excess) sum_{w in R\{u,v}} |D(u,v,w)| = sum over dominators x of {u,v} of #{w in R\{u,v}, x -> w}. An x in R beats 5 vertices of R, two of them u, v: contributes 3. A y in O with u,v in M_y beats |M_y| - 2 = 4 - e_y further vertices of R. Total 3c + 4K - E_both = 4|D| - c - E_both (K = #y). Subtract 9*5: s(u,v) = 4|D(u,v)| - c - 45 - E_both >= 0 by (F1). Justified.
(Ex) sum over the 45 triples through u of |D| = sum over dominators x of u of C(#out-neighbours of x in R other than u, 2) = 5*C(4,2) + sum_{y : u in M_y} C(|M_y| - 1, 2) = 30 + sum C(10 - q_y, 2). With C(10-q,2) = 10 - lambda(q) and (I1): Ex(u) = 30 + 10(20 + j_u) - sum lambda - 225 = 5 + 10 j_u - sum_{y : u in M_y} lambda(q_y). (A y with q_y = 11 has M_y empty and never appears, so lambda(11) is irrelevant.) Justified.
(Lemma T, recovered) Ex(u) >= 0 and lambda >= 0 give 10 j_u >= -5, so j_u >= 0: every dominator of a tight pair has in-degree >= 25. This is the same identity, so j_r >= 0 needs no separate input.
(Sum s) Each triple {u,v,w} through u is counted in s(u,v) and s(u,w): sum_v s(u,v) = 2Ex(u); termwise nonnegativity gives s(u,v) <= min(Ex(u), Ex(v)). Justified.
(Pair-sum) sum_{v != u} c(u,v) = 5 in-neighbours * 4 = 20; sum_v #{y : u,v in M_y} = sum_{y : u in M_y} (|M_y| - 1) = 5(20 + j_u) - tau_u. So sum_{v != u} |D(u,v)| = 120 + 5 j_u - tau_u. Justified.
(Lemma A at N = 52) Let j_u = 0. Ex(u) = 5 - sum lambda >= 0. A y with q_y in {7,8,9,10} and u in M_y contributes lambda >= 7 > 5; a y with q_y = 11 has M_y empty. So u in Q_y whenever q_y >= 7, and at most one y0 with q = 6 has u in M_{y0} (two would give 8 > 5). Let beta = [y0 exists], m(v) = [v in M_{y0}]; sum_{v != u} m(v) = |M_{y0}| - 1 = 4 beta. Every other y with u in M_y has e_y = 0, so E_both(u,v) = m(v). Then s(u,v) = 4|D| - c - 45 - m == 3 - c - m (mod 4). Since 0 <= c <= 4 and m <= 1, a nonnegative integer in this class is >= 3 - c - m if c + m <= 3 and >= 7 - c - m if c + m in {4,5}. Summing: sum_v s(u,v) >= 30 - 20 - 4 beta + 4 N_4 = 10 - 4 beta + 4 N_4. But sum_v s = 2Ex(u) = 10 - 8 beta. Hence beta = N_4 = 0 and every inequality is tight: s(u,v) = 3 - c(u,v), c(u,v) <= 3, and |D(u,v)| = (3 - c + c + 45)/4 = 12 for every v. With beta = 0, u lies in Q_y for every heavy y. Justified (Lemma A does not use c >= 1).
Consequence: every heavy y has M_y inside V_+, |M_y| = 6 - e_y <= s, so e_y >= 6 - s; for u in V_+ the 11 - s pairs into V_0 have 12 dominators, so sum_{v in V_+\u} |D(u,v)| = 12(s - 1) + 5 j_u - tau_u; every pair has |D| >= 12 (4|D| >= 45 + c + E_both >= 45); and s(u,v) >= 4|D| - 49 - E_both.
(c >= 1) For u,v in R the 4-set {a,b,u,v} has a dominator w outside it (S_4). Arc directions: w -> a, w -> b, w -> u, w -> v. From w -> a and w -> b, w in D(P) = R; w is not u or v. So w is a common in-neighbour of u and v in R: c(u,v) >= 1, i.e. T[R] has S_2. Justified. With s >= 0 this gives |D(u,v)| >= ceil((46 + E_both)/4), so >= 13 when E_both >= 3.

STEP 1b. J <= 2 directly at N = 52 (closes G1, removes the dependence on Lemma J). J = 0: V_+ empty, every heavy has e = 6, and 6 does not divide 14. J = 1: s = 1, e in {5,6}, and 13 is not a sum of 5s and 6s. J = 2, s = 1 (j = 2): e in {5,6}, 12 = 6+6 only; q = 11 vertices miss nothing, tau = 0, and the pair-sum with no V_+ partner reads 0 = 5*2 - 0, false. J = 2, s = 2 (1,1): e in {4,5,6}, 12 = 6+6 or 4+4+4. For 6+6: tau = 0, the single pair has |D| = 12 + 5 = 17, E_both = 0, s = 23 - c >= 19 > Ex = 15. For 4+4+4: the three q = 9 vertices miss both, lambda sum 30 > 15. So J <= 2 is impossible.

STEP 2. research/N52_TIGHT_J_GE_6.md.
Section 1 (lines 10-21). The c >= 1 proof is correct (Step 1). The R4-C survivor: |D(C,D)| = 12, E_both(C,D) = 3, s(C,D) = 48 - c - 45 - 3 = -c, so c(C,D) = 0, contradicting c >= 1. Justified. Section 1 depends on R4-C's claim that this is the unique pair-level survivor at J = 5, s = 4; I re-derived that classification. j = (2,1,1,1) (only composition of 5 into four parts); E = 9; tau_A <= 10, tau_deg1 <= 5. Partitions of 9 into parts 2..6: 6+3, 5+4, 5+2+2, 4+3+2, 3+3+3, 3+2+2+2 (complete). 3+3+3: sum tau = 27 > 25. 3+2+2+2: every tau >= 6. 4+3+2: if M_3 = {B,C,D} every 2-set meets a degree-1 vertex with tau 5, giving 9; if M_3 contains A and misses D, tau = (5,5,5,2) and every 2-set raises B, C to 9 or D to 6. 5+2+2: the 5 must sit on A, Ex = 1 everywhere, the six V_+ counts sum to 74, E_both = 4 on every pair, so |D| = 12 is negative excess and |D| >= 14 exceeds Ex = 1; all six would be 13 = 78 > 74. 5+4: both on A gives |D(C,D)| = |D(A,B)| + 4 in {16, 17}: 16 forces |D(A,B)| = 12 with E_both 4 (negative), 17 has s >= 19 > 15. Disjoint with 5 on A: |D(A,B)| = |D(C,D)| + 4, |D(C,D)| = 13 forces |D(A,B)| = 17, s >= 19 > 15. 4 on A: B's three pairs are 12, then AC = 13, AD = 17, CD = 12, s(A,D) >= 19 > 15. Neither on A: |D(Y,Z)| = 8. 6+3 with A untouched: triangle on B,C,D sums to 34 < 36. 6+3 with B untouched: CD = AB - 4, AC = BD + 1, AD = BC + 1, BC + BD + CD = 37 = {13,12,12}; CD = 13 gives AB = 17, s >= 19 > Ex(B) = 15; otherwise CD = 12 with E_both = 3 forces c(C,D) = 0. So with c >= 1, J = 5, s = 4 is empty. Justified.
Section 2 (lines 24-50). Tools: pair-sum 53 - tau_u over the four V_+ partners (6 pairs into V_0 at 12) - correct; tau_u <= 5 - correct; Ex(u) = 15 - sum lambda - correct; |D| >= ceil((46 + E_both)/4) - correct. Partition filter: computed independently (r8a_checks.py): the partitions of 9 into parts <= 6 admitting a labelled placement on five vertices with every tau <= 5 are exactly 6+3, 6+2+1, 6+1+1+1, 5+4, 5+2+2, 4+4+1, as printed. The printed reasons are right: 5+3+1, 5+2+1+1, 5+1^4 put tau = 6 on the 5's vertex (the 1 misses all five); 4+3+2 has sum tau = 25 so needs tau = 5 everywhere, but 5 = 3 + 2 is the only decomposition and only three vertices lie in M_3. 6+3: pair sums 50,50,50,53,53; internal pairs >= 13 force internal = 13 and cross = 12; {w1,w2} gets 53 - 36 = 17, s = 23 - c >= 19 > 15. Justified. 6+2+1: four vertices with sum 50, six internal pairs E_both = 3 so >= 78, but 2I = 4*50 - 52 = 148, I = 74. Justified. 6+1+1+1: all E_both = 3, total >= 130 vs 125. Justified. 5+4: x (missed by the 5) has four pairs 12; x is not in M_4 because tau_x <= 5 (unstated, G3); {y,z} has E_both = 4 so >= 13; y's sum 49 = 12 + 13 + 12 + 12 forces the rest; w1w2 = 53 - 36 = 17, s >= 19 > 15. Justified. 5+2+2: tau_x <= 5 forces both M_2 = V_+ \ x (unstated, G3); the four have sum 49, pair to x is 12, three internal pairs with E_both = 4 each >= 13 sum to >= 39 > 37. Justified. 4+4+1: tau <= 5 forces disjoint M_4's (unstated, G3); a vertex in an M_4 has tau = 5, sum 48, but its M_4-partner pair has E_both = 5, >= 13: 49 > 48. Justified. Line 47 'So J = 5 is impossible' is correct only together with R3-C (s <= 3) and section 1 (s = 4); s = 5 is all section 2 treats (G2). Line 47 'With R1-C (J >= 5)': R1-C's J <= 2 rests on Lemma J; Step 1b replaces that.

STEP 3. R1-C (J = 3, J = 4) re-derived case by case. J = 3, E = 11: s = 1 (6+5): 5j = 15 != tau = 5. s = 2: only 6+5; q = 10 on the j = 1 vertex gives 12 vs 22, on the j = 2 vertex gives |D| = 17, E_both = 0, s >= 19 > Ex = 15. s = 3: 6+5 gives D12 = D13 = 12, D23 = 17, s >= 19 > 15; 5+3+3 lambda 18 > 15; 4+4+3 lambda >= 19 > 15. J = 4, E = 10: s = 1 (5+5): tau = 10 != 20. s = 2: (2,2) 6+4 gives |D| = 18, E_both = 4, s >= 19 > 15; (3,1) 6+4 gives 23 vs 13; (2,2) 5+5 forces one each, |D| = 17, s >= 19 > 15; (3,1) 5+5 forces both on the j = 3 vertex, |D| = 17, s >= 19 > Ex = 15. s = 3 (2,1,1): 4+3+3 lambda 18 > 15; 6+4 missing the two j = 1: D23 = 8; missing s1 and s2: D13 = 17 with E_both 0, s >= 19 > Ex(s3) = 15; 5+5 all five placements (s1s1: D23 = 17; s2s2: lambda 20 > 15; s2s3: D23 = 7; s1s2 and s1s3: a pair of 17 with E_both 0 against Ex 15). s = 4 (1,1,1,1), the nine partitions 6+4, 5+5, 6+2+2, 5+3+2, 4+4+2, 4+3+3, 4+2+2+2, 3+3+2+2, 2^5: 6+4 gives CD = AB + 4 >= 16, 16 makes AB = 12 with E_both 4 (negative), >= 17 makes s >= 19 > 15; 5+5 distinct gives CD = 17; 6+2+2 sum 74 forces a 12 with E_both 4; the rest die by lambda (16, 17, 18, 21, 18, 35 > 15). All as written in R1-C after its own corrections. Justified.
R3-C (J = 5, s <= 3) re-derived. s = 1: 9 is not a sum of 5s and 6s. s = 2: only 5+4, consistency forces j = (3,2) with the 5 on the 3, |D| = 18, E_both 4, s >= 19 > Ex = 15. s = 3: 3+3+3 lambda 27 > 15 at the part 1; 6+3 gives D opposite i = 23 - 5 j_i: (3,1,1) gives 8, (2,2,1) gives 18 on the degree-2 pair with s >= 20 > 16; 5+4 with the 5 on Z gives D_XY = 23 - 5 j_Z, and the sub-cases (j_Z >= 3: <= 8; j_Z = 1 with (2,2): 18, s >= 19 > 15; j_Z = 1 with (3,1): 7; j_Z = 2: 17 against 15); 5+4 with the 5 on X gives D_YZ = 27 - 5 j_X, j_X in {2,3}, sub-cases 17 vs 15, 8, 17 vs 15. Justified. R3-C's J >= 6 part is not needed for J <= 5 and was not audited.
Chain: J <= 2 (Step 1b), J = 3, 4 (R1-C), J = 5 with s <= 3 (R3-C), s = 4 (R4-C + section 1), s = 5 (section 2). s <= J, so this covers every case. Therefore J <= 5 is impossible.

STEP 4. research/compute/n52_pairlevel.py, row by row. arc[u,v] Bool means u -> v; out-degree 5 per vertex gives the 5-regular T[R] (justified, Step 1(0)); c[u,v] = #w with arc[w,u] and arc[w,v] = common in-neighbours, domain [1,4] (c >= 1 by S_4 on {a,b,u,v}; c <= 4 by in-degree 5). heavy_sets = subsets of pos (= V_+) of size 0..5, i.e. e = 6 - |M| in 1..6: restriction to V_+ is exactly Lemma A ('u in Q_y for every heavy y when j_u = 0'); size 0 (q = 11) included. n[M] in [0, 14 - J] (valid since 6 - |M| >= 1); sum n[M](6 - |M|) = 14 - J (Lemma I at N = 52). nlight + nheavy = 39. Ex[u] = 5 + 10 j_u - sum n[M] lambda(11 - |M|), domain [0, 5 + 10 j_u] (Ex >= 0; upper bound implied). L[u] + #heavy containing u = 20 + j_u (I1 split into light and heavy); sum L = 6 nlight (light |M_y| = 6). D[u,v] in [12, 43] (12 from 4D >= 45; 43 = 4 + 39). k[u,v] in [0,39]. D = c + k + #heavy containing u,v (pair identity). s = 4D - c - 45 - sum n[M](6 - |M|) over heavy M containing u,v (triple excess; light have e = 0). s domain [0, 5 + 10 max(j_u, j_v)]: valid but looser than min; s <= Ex[u], s <= Ex[v] (the binding rows). sum_v s = 2Ex[u]. sum_v k = 5 L[u] (each light y with u in M_y has 5 other misses). sum_v D = 120 + 5 j_u - tau_u (pair-sum). For u in V_0: c <= 3 and D = 12 (Lemma A). Labelling: the j-vector is placed on vertices 0..len-1 with T[R] free, which is without loss of generality. partitions(J, J, 11) enumerates all partitions of J into at most 11 parts. Every row is a valid consequence of S_4 at N = 52; no row is unjustified. Operational notes only: default workers = 8 exceeds the 3-worker budget (I reran with 3); main() overwrites n52_pairlevel_{J}_{J}.json; INFEASIBLE is CP-SAT output without a certificate.

solver_free_enumeration.domain: J = 0..5, every j-partition placed on V_+, every multiset of heavy miss-sets inside V_+ with sum e = 14 - J, every integer dominator count on V_+ pairs; rows: Ex >= 0, pair-sum 12(s-1) + 5j - tau, |D| >= 12, exists c in [cmin,4] with 0 <= 4D - c - 45 - E_both <= min Ex

survivors_cmin_0.(2,1,1,1): 3 labelled placements, all 6+3 with the q = 8 missing the degree-2 vertex and two degree-1 vertices (the R4-C pattern)

weaknesses: Status proved is unreviewed. (F1), every triple has >= 5 dominators, is taken from proof/ERDOS902_PROOF.md Lemma 1.2 and not re-proved. The audit re-derived the hand arguments; it did not find an error, which is evidence but not a guarantee that a second human reader would agree on every arithmetic step. The enumeration and the hand proofs share the same identities, so the numerical identity check on planted random instances is the only test of the identities that is independent of their derivation, and it tests only the double-counting parts (not (F1), Lemma A or c >= 1). R3-C's J >= 6 part, R4-C's witness data for c >= 0, and the full local models (n52_full.py etc.) were not audited. The CP-SAT verdicts carry no certificate. The result concerns tight pairs at order 52 with J <= 5 only: tight pairs with 6 <= J <= 14 and the no-tight branch remain open, so f(4) >= 53 is not proved and Erdos 902 is not solved.
